brief:
Commentator Peter Beinart argues that defenders of Israel invoke Palestinian voting rights selectively, according to Zeteo. They highlight Palestinian participation in Israeli elections as evidence of democratic practice while remaining silent when Israeli authorities move to curtail or eliminate that voting access, he contends.

Beinart characterizes this rhetorical approach as using Palestinian voters as "window dressing"—highlighting their presence to counter criticism while ignoring substantive threats to their electoral participation. The pattern, he suggests, allows Israel's international boosters to claim democratic credentials without addressing contradictions in how voting rights are actually implemented.
dek: Peter Beinart explains how Israel’s boosters laud it for allowing some Palestinians to vote – and stay silent when Israel tries to take that vote away.
title: Israel's supporters cite Palestinian voting rights while ignoring restrictions, Beinart says
